name: BakeBase v1.5 - Release Candidate
body:
# BakeBase v1.5 — Release Candidate

BakeBase v1.5 prepares the home-bakery manager for public beta testing. This release adds editing of existing orders and a shorter completion command, improves client-name handling, and fixes issues found during alpha testing. It also refreshes the interface and guides while retaining the catalogue search, order filters, deadline sorting, command history, and single-step undo introduced in v1.4.

## What's new since v1.4

- **Edit existing orders:** use `edit-order CONTACT_INDEX o/ORDER_INDEX [i/ITEM_INDEX] [q/QUANTITY] [d/DEADLINE]` to correct an order's item, quantity, deadline, or any combination of these fields. Omitted fields remain unchanged. The order keeps its client, identity, completion status, and client-local number; identical repeat orders remain separate.
- **Shorter completion command:** `mark CONTACT_INDEX o/ORDER_INDEX` is now an alias for `mark-order-complete`. Both spellings share the same validation, saving, and undo behavior.
- **More flexible client names:** printable ASCII punctuation is accepted in names, including apostrophes, hyphens, periods, and slashes. Names such as `Anne-Marie O'Neil` and `Siti d/o Rahim` can be entered without removing their punctuation.
- **Possible-duplicate warnings:** adding or editing a client warns when another name matches after ignoring case and repeated spaces. The operation succeeds and keeps the supplied spelling; records are not merged automatically. Exact-name duplicates are still rejected.
- **Corrected email validation:** allowed adjacent local-part symbols and internal domain hyphens are handled consistently. Examples include `alice+_orders@example.com` and `alice@xn--bcher-kva.de`; consecutive local-part periods remain invalid.
- **Startup recovery for null JSON:** a data file containing only `null` now follows the existing loading-error recovery path instead of crashing startup. An invalid bakery book starts empty, while null preferences fall back to defaults.
- **More complete and accessible Help:** the command summary now includes completed and incomplete order filters and their `by-deadline` option. Reopening Help also restores it when minimized and brings it into focus.
- **Command-only undo:** the main-window Undo button has been removed. Type `undo` to recover the last successfully saved data change.
- **Updated release documentation:** corrected quick-start commands, explained the working-directory data-file location, refreshed the main UI image and DG diagrams, and replaced the obsolete claim that order deletion was unimplemented.

## Important behavior notes

- Client and item indices refer to their **currently displayed lists**. Order indices refer to the selected client's **full order list**, including orders hidden by order searches or completion filters. Use the refreshed displayed indices after filtering.
- Editing an order preserves active order searches, completion filters, and deadline sorting. The edited order may move in a sorted view or leave a search result when its details change.
- Undo remains single-step, has no redo, and is cleared on restart. A successful order edit can be undone; submitting unchanged values does not replace the previous undo opportunity.
- A possible-duplicate warning means the client was added or edited successfully. Run `undo` immediately if that change was accidental.
- Client names must contain printable ASCII characters; Chinese characters and curly apostrophes are not supported. Reserved command-prefix sequences cannot be entered literally where the parser interprets them as fields; see the User Guide.
- Item and order searches continue to match whole words, case-insensitively, with OR semantics across keywords. Punctuation remains part of a word.
- `clear` shows a warning and counts. `clear confirm` deletes all records immediately without another prompt. Back up valuable data before clearing, populating, or manually editing JSON.
- Data is stored at `data/addressbook.json` relative to the folder from which you launch the app. Use one running instance per data folder; simultaneous sessions do not synchronize their changes.

## Feature highlights

### Clients, catalogue, and orders together

The current interface keeps all three panels visible and uses order colors to distinguish completed, incomplete, and overdue orders. Undo is available through the command input.

![BakeBase v1.5 showing clients, bakery items, and colored order cards](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/releases/download/v1.5/01-bakery-overview-v1.5.png)

### Correct an order without recreating it

With the preloaded sample book and all clients displayed, change only the quantity of client 1's second order:

```text
edit-order 1 o/2 q/13
```

Its other details and completion status remain unchanged. Run `undo` immediately to restore the previous quantity.

### Mark an order using the shorter command

To mark client 2's first sample order complete:

```text
mark 2 o/1
```

The longer `mark-order-complete 2 o/1` spelling remains supported. Use `unmark 2 o/1` to restore it to incomplete.

### Focus on upcoming work

The existing completion filter and deadline sort remain available together:

```text
list-incomplete-orders by-deadline
```

This lists incomplete orders from earliest deadline to latest. It sorts by deadline; it does not filter by a date cutoff. Run `list-orders` to restore the complete insertion-order view.

## Download and run

1. Install Java 25 or later and check it with `java -version`.
2. Download [BakeBase-v1.5.jar](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-3/tp/releases/download/v1.5/BakeBase-v1.5.jar) and place it in a writable folder.
3. Open a terminal, change to that folder, and run:

```text
java -jar BakeBase-v1.5.jar
```

A fresh data folder loads the sample book with 12 clients, 12 bakery items, and 24 orders. `populate` replaces existing data with a new sample book; it does not append records. Close the app before manually editing or replacing its data files.

## Validation

Built from team commit `e449792e137b14dcb3017da2c688d2a71f677a25`. All **579 automated tests**, Gradle checks, and repository checks passed locally on Windows with Java 25. The packaged JAR passed fresh-start and null-JSON recovery startup smoke checks. The corrected quick-start and DG deletion examples were checked through the real parser, model, and disposable JSON storage. The updated product website deployed successfully.

```text

```
